comparison.objective: Safely dismantle an opened battery pack by removing a service plug, proving de-energization, then removing busbars and nuts; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber for acceptable repeated stopping behavior.
comparison.physical_skill: Battery work involves service-plug extraction, live-dead-live meter probing, insulated-driver use, nut removal, and collision-free busbar transfer. Candidate centers on recessed key insertion, bimanual counterholding, collar adjustment, bounded locking torque, and feedback-driven iteration.
comparison.success_condition: PR requires the safety sequence before nut turning and removal of two busbars and four nuts without bridging terminals. It provides no numeric torque, clearance, dwell, or partial-score rubric and has no spec versions. Candidate instead imposes numeric impact-energy, velocity, 12 mm stroke, repeatability, rebound, overload, hard-stop, and lock-drift checks.
comparison.reason: Some tool alignment and turning primitives are shared, but the objectives, manipulation sequence, hazards, and measured outcomes are substantially different. Missing numeric PR thresholds do not plausibly make this unrelated battery-disassembly task a duplicate.
